accuracy.evidence: Checked against USDA NRCS conservation practice standards (Windbreak/Shelterbelt Establishment code 380, Terrace code 600, Critical Area Planting code 342), the Universal Soil Loss Equation cover-management factor (C about 1.0 for bare fallow, about 0.01–0.05 for dense grass sod), National Geographic's 'Erosion' entry and BGS coastal-erosion pages. Erosion is defined as material carried away by water, wind or ice; plant cover reduces raindrop splash and roots bind soil; terraces shorten slope length and slow runoff; a toe wall retains soil that moves but does not stop wear upslope; windbreak protection extends roughly 10 times the barrier height downwind and the barrier must be upwind; marram grass and sand fences trap blowing sand on dunes. The tray grams are labelled as model numbers in both the lab data comment and the adult text, and only their order is claimed to match field studies.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets mistakes reported in NGSS 2-ESS2-1 teaching notes and primary fair-testing research: plants help because they drink the rain (Dee, m2), a windbreak can go on either side (step 3 predict options 'side the wind blows to' and 'middle', p3, challenge tag side, the downwind and in-field hedge feedback), a wall stops erosion everywhere (m5, tag wall, the wall result showing 30 g still lost), sweeping the road instead of fixing the dune (FIX round 2, m4, tag sweep), bare soil 'stays where it is' (step 1 predict) and unfair tests that give one fix more rain (Gia, p5, m9, tag fair).

lab_distinct.evidence: gate_lab_distinct passed (under 30% similar to every flagship lab, including flagcolony committed earlier this run). The related lab 617 flagfastslow shows erosion happening (scrubbing soft rock, drip-wear) but never compares solutions. This lab is about prevention: dragging a rain cloud over four covers with equal rain and reading soil in a catch tray, and dragging a hedge whose calm-air zone (10 times its height) must cover a field downwind. Neither mechanism appears in another lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: The learner picks each cover and makes the same amount of rain fall (the rain meter must reach 100% every time), and the catch tray fills to 80 g, 30 g, 20 g or 10 g, so 'plants hold the soil best' and 'the wall only catches soil at the bottom' are read from their own results before the step text confirms them. Dragging the hedge shows a live '% of the field sheltered' and blowing dust only over the unsheltered part, so placing it upwind and close enough is discovered, and the text then names the 10-times-height rule.

predictions.evidence: Step 1 asks where the soil on a bare hill goes, with 'It stays where it is' as the tempting answer, disproved by the water and wind cards. Step 2 asks which hill loses least, with 'They all lose the same' and 'Bare soil' as the tempting answers, disproved by the 80 g versus 10 g catch trays. Step 3 asks where the hedge goes, with 'On the side the wind blows to' tempting; the lab starts the hedge on that side, showing only 29% sheltered and dust blowing until it is moved upwind.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Each challenge distractor has a tag with its own message: bare ('no leaves soften the rain and no roots hold the soil'), fair ('Change only one thing, the cover'), side ('so the wind is slowed before it reaches the field'), roots, wall ('the hill above still wears') and sweep ('Fix the cause'). In the lab, a wrong sort explains what carries that material, each wrong fix explains why it fails (e.g. ploughing loosens soil), and a misplaced hedge gets one of three messages: past the field, inside the field with the % sheltered, or too far upwind.

readability.evidence: learn/readability.py gives the kid text grade 2.3 (limit 6.5) and the adult text grade 9.2 (limit 9.5). Kid sentences are short and concrete ('Their roots grip the soil like a net'); 'erosion', 'terraces' and 'windbreak' are each explained where they first appear; lab buttons use plain verbs ('Make it rain', 'Hedge left').

no_filler.evidence: gate_content found no filler phrases. Each kid paragraph carries a fact the lab tests (what erosion is, how plants help, terraces and walls, windbreak side plus fair testing); the adult text gives the standards, the five tasks, a note that tray grams are model figures, and named mistakes, with no repeated template wording.

mobile.evidence: Screenshots at 360 px (Android, light and dark) and 1200 px desktop: four cover tiles fit in one row with their gram results, the cloud is limited to the hill so it never covers the rain meter or catch tray labels, the hill, wall and terraces are drawn clearly, the windbreak scene shows wind labels, the sheltered % at the top and the 'calm air' label clamped inside the canvas, and the fix and kid cards wrap to two lines without clipping. All actions have full-size buttons under the canvas.

accessibility.evidence: gate_browser passed: axe (WCAG 2.1 AA) clean in both themes on desktop and iPhone 13, every task completes with Show me, no console errors. Every drag has a button route (Water/Wind, 'Try: <cover>' and 'Make it rain', 'Hedge left/right', one button per fix or child), and the canvas aria-label is rewritten after each action with the card, the tray, the rain % and all results so far, or the field span, hedge position and % sheltered.
